sentences.text: Largirostrornis is classified as a genus of enantiornithean bird, a group belonging to the family Cuspirostrisornithidae.
In 1997, it was known to possess the longest torso of any described Enantiornithes, with a skull measuring approximately 32 millimeters in length.
Its paired dentaries and premaxillae each contained six teeth, and the bird possessed tall neural spines on its cervical and dorsal vertebrae.
Largirostrornis held the record for the longest torso among all described Enantiornithes when it was first described.
The species name sexdentoris reflects the unique feature of having exactly six teeth in its upper and lower jaw bones.

The only known fossil is a slab and counterslab found in the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning province, China. The holotype specimen, cataloged as IVPP 10531, is held at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing. The species Largirostrornis sexdentoris was named and described by Hou Lianhai in 1997.

Largirostrornis lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the late Aptian age, approximately 120.3 ±0.7 million years ago. The time range for the genus is recorded as the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
Some researchers debate whether Largirostrornis sexdentoris is a distinct species or a junior synonym of Cathayornis yandica.
